title: Wright-Patterson AFB Federal Facility Agreement (CERCLA §120)
warnings: Source is an OCR'd scan of the 1991 FFA; the OCR is garbled in places ("PwwLcuu" = Program, "cxarvleted" = completed). Dates, statutory citations, and the Findings of Fact were read against context; verbatim quotes above are normalized only where OCR mangled obvious words.

The administrative docket number is blank on the executed cover sheet in this copy. The document's own metadata keyword is "3/31/91" (the execution/signature date); the FFA becomes formally EFFECTIVE only when U.S. EPA issues its post-public-comment notice (Section 40), a date not stated in this copy — recorded here as execution_date, not effective_date.

fields.agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region V (and U.S. Department of the Air Force)
fields.program: CERCLA Section 120 Federal Facility Agreement (Superfund; DoD Installation Restoration Program)
fields.applicant: United States Department of the Air Force (Wright-Patterson AFB)
fields.site_address: Wright-Patterson AFB, Miami River Valley Basin northeast of Dayton, Greene and Montgomery Counties, Ohio — approx. 8,200 acres ("Areas A and C" and "Area B")
fields.affected_resource: Miami Buried Valley Aquifer (the sole-source drinking-water aquifer; 17 WPAFB supply wells + Dayton/Fairborn municipal well fields) contaminated by VOCs (TCE, PCE, carbon tetrachloride, 1,1,1-TCA, chloroform, 1,2-DCE, toluene) from ≥58 base waste-disposal sites.
fields.note: The CERCLA Section 120 Federal Facility Agreement between U.S. EPA Region V and the U.S. Air Force governing Superfund cleanup at WPAFB. Executed 1991 (metadata 3/31/91), following the base's NPL listing on 1989-10-04 (54 Fed. Reg. 41021). Findings of Fact tie the contamination directly to the Miami Buried Valley Aquifer — the SAME sole-source aquifer designated at 53 FR 15876 (see ssa-53fr15876.epa.yaml). This is the [verified] primary instrument behind the WPAFB profile's TCE/PFAS-plume receiving-water dimension.

title: Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS), Sole Source Aquifer Petition
warnings: The primary source is a 2006 U.S. EPA Region 5 full-text TRANSCRIPTION of the Federal Register notice ("Not Original Document"), not the original Federal Register page image. All figures below are transcribed verbatim from that transcription.

The petition designated the ENTIRE Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS) across nine counties; "Great Miami North" in the source filename is the Ohio-EPA source-water map segment label, not a separate designation. WPAFB (Greene + Montgomery) sits within the designated area.

fields.agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region V
fields.program: Sole Source Aquifer designation under SDWA Section 1424(e)
fields.applicant: Miami Valley Regional Planning Commission (Dayton, Ohio)
fields.project_name: Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS), Sole Source Aquifer Petition
fields.site_address: Great Miami / Little Miami River Basins, Southwestern Ohio (Preble, Dark, Champaign, Miami, Montgomery, Logan, Clark, Greene and Shelby Counties)
fields.affected_resource: Buried Valley Aquifer System — the sole or principal drinking-water source for the petitioned area; all Federal financially assisted projects in the aquifer area and its principal recharge zone become subject to EPA project review under SDWA 1424(e).
fields.note: U.S. EPA Region V final determination designating the Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS) of the Great Miami/Little Miami River Basins of southwestern Ohio a SOLE SOURCE AQUIFER under SDWA Section 1424(e) (42 U.S.C. 300f, 300h-3(e)), signed by Regional Administrator Valdas V. Adamkus on 1988-04-14, published at 53 Fed. Reg. 15876 (May 4, 1988), FR Doc. 88-9103. Petition submitted by the Miami Valley Regional Planning Commission (complete petition received 1987-11-25); public comment 1987-12-22 through 1988-02-22 drew a single comment, in support. This is the [verified] primary instrument behind the WPAFB profile's sole-source-aquifer claim: the base's drinking-water and plume story rests on this aquifer.
